characters.name: In General
characters.description: Affably Evil: Despite being unrepentantly evil supervillains that freely kill and rape however they please, they are all chummy with each other sometimes to the point ofVillains Out Shopping. Allegorical Character: They are a collective one for theThe Dark Age of Comic Books, being responsible for the world's lack of true superheroes, its grim and grittiness, and all of this beginning inThe '80swhere the Dark Age is said to begin. Their defeat at the end ofBig Game (2023)is meant to beMark Millar's call for a return to more traditional and hopeful superheroics overDarker and Edgierstories. Ancient Conspiracy: Amusingly, they act like this but they really only formed inThe '80s. Asshole Victim: Anytime any one of them dies, remember that no one in the Fraternity deserves any sympathy because they are all unrepentant supervillains who rape and kill with zero remorse and are secretly controlling the world. The Bad Guys Win: They are what happens when all the rogues galleries of each superhero joined forces to kill them all.

characters.name: Wesley Gibson
characters.description: Adrenaline Makeover: Wesley trades in his jeans/t-shirts/windbreaker style for tailored three-piece suits. Beard of Evil: Rocks an evil goatee upon his return inNemesis: Reloaded. Being Evil Sucks: In spite of being very much into being a supervillain, Wesley admits after massacring a police station that being evil all the time wears one out, and makes him question whether he truly wants to stay in this life for but a brief moment. Fox assures him that it's rather normal to get burnt out on being evil and advises him to learn to discipline himself. Big Bad: OfBig Game (2023). Blood Knight:He kills for the thrill of it. HisRoaring Rampage of Revengeis less about avenging Seltzer, his father, or even the Fraternity friends he's made, but rather the adrenaline high he's getting from massacring all of Rictus's mooks.Wesley isn't bothered byHit-Girl time travelling to rescue all the heroes, because he gets to live his generation's ownFinal Battleagainst superheroes and kill them personally.

characters.name: The Killer
characters.description: Acrofatic: He gained a bit of a gut in his old age, but is still able to jump and shoot like an athlete. Age-Gap Romance: He was in an occasional sexual relationship with the Fox since she was fourteen. Boom, Headshot!: He's shot in the head by averylong-range sniper rifle.Or so Fox claims. Comic-Book Fantasy Casting: He looks a lot likeTommy Lee Jones. Death Seeker:His realization that his age was catching up to him drives him to plot out his son's succession of him and to put a bullet into him before he truly entersHow the Mighty Have Fallenterritory.

characters.name: The Fox
characters.description: Animal Motifs: It's in her name. Comic-Book Fantasy Casting: Drawn to resembleHalle Berry, who would go on to portray Fox's inspiration Catwoman in hereponymous 2004 film. Dating Catwoman: True to her inspiration, the Killer notes that Fox used to be the villainess lover of their mutual superhero enemy. Demoted to Extra: She was a major supporting character inWantedbut is barely even a presence inBig Game (2023). Corrupted Character Copy: Fox is one forCatwoman. Both are cunningClassy Cat Burglarswith an animal motif and an implied romantic relationship with"The Dectective". However, while Catwoman is aNoble Demonat worst and often an outrightAnti-Hero, avoiding causing serious harm or stealing from those who can't afford it, Fox is an amoral and ruthless murderer whoseEstablishing Character Momentis gunning down an entire diner purely to prove she's not scared of the police.

characters.name: Professor Seltzer
characters.description: Affably Evil: He's nothing but courteous with Wesley, and was the mastermind behind the deaths of all the superheroes. Arch-Enemy: His wasThe Capeof the previous universe. Asshole Victim: His death scene is directly preceded by him wanting to see some underage prostitutes. Battle Trophy: In the aftermath of theFinal Battleagainst the superheroes and before rewriting reality, Seltzer found thered capeof his nemesis and secretly kept it as a trophy despite having agreed to erase all evidence of the heroes' existence. Brainy Baby: According to theWanted Dossier, he was able to talk in the womb and was able to read and solve math problems before he could walk.

characters.name: Mr. Rictus
characters.description: Bestiality Is Depraved: He doesn't deny Wesley's snark about him fucking goats. He only takes issue with it because he insists that he "makes love" to them instead. Big Bad: OfWanted. His desires to wreak havoc on the world drives him to turn on Seltzer and take over the Fraternity. He's also suspected of killing Wesley's father as part of his gambit to take over.He didn't. Bring It: His reaction to being warned by Adam-One that his actions might attract unwanted attention from the superheroes of the multiverse. Death by Origin Story: Invoked on the fly. After randomly killing a child's parents in front of him, he just shrugs and decides to let it inspire the kid to train and seek revenge so he can have a new enemy to fight. Defiant to the End:At Wesley's mercy and bleeding out from a bullet to the neck, Rictus just gives an extremely sarcastic answer to Wesley's demands to know who killed his father right before Wesley ends him. "LEE HARVEY OSWALD!"

characters.name: Doll-Master
characters.description: Adorable Evil Minions: The Doll-Master uses robot dolls to commit crimes. Affably Evil: Is the most polite and easy-going of Seltzer's Fraternity faction. Beware the Nice Ones: Despite his nice demeanor, he's ultimately still a supervillain.When he learns that Rictus had his family murdered, he unleashes his toys on him and his men, eliciting fear from the otherwiseAx-Crazyvillain for a moment. Comic-Book Fantasy Casting: Is noted to look likeMark Hamill, who is known for toy collecting. Creepy Doll: The Doll-Master's weapons of choice. Able to fly and loaded with Professor Seltzer-designed weapons.

characters.name: Fuckwit
characters.description: Dumbass No More: As lampshaded by Sucker, Fuckwit surprisingly became more talkative in his final hours, even forgoing the backwards way of speaking he had throughout the comic.It ends up not mattering as he's beaten to death shortly after it's noted. Dumb Muscle: His mental disability has caused him some issues with his intelligence, and he's one of the physically strongest members of the Fraternity. Expy: Of Bizarro, given that he's a mentally deficient clone of the setting'sSuperman Substituteand follows a backwards sense of logic. Flying Brick: As a clone of the world's greatest superhero, Fuckwit inherited his flight, strength, and invulnerability. Puppy-Dog Eyes:Gives a look of utter pathetic helplessness at Johnny Two-Dicks, who reluctantly beats him to death.

characters.name: Imp
characters.description: All There in the Manual: Him actually being a baby by seventh dimensional standards and the fact that he's having an affair with Deadly Nightshade is only spoken of in theWanted Dossier. Brought Down to Badass: During Rictus's coup, the Future manages to summon Imp to their dimension and depower him, but he still manages to maintain enough power to fight them to a stalement untilSucker flies through him at super speed. Enfant Terrible: He's actually a baby by seventh dimension standards despite being thousands of Earth years old. Expy: Of Mr. Mxyzptlk, given that he's a reality-warping imp from another dimension. Great Gazoo: An impish creature who can bend reality in cartoonish ways, much like his inspiration.

characters.name: Sucker
characters.description: All There in the Manual: Him being an alien parasite that hops from host to host is not mentioned at all in the main comic. Cigar Chomper: Can be seen enjoying Cuban cigars. TheDossierquips that it's reflective of how he leaves his host bodies: dried up husks. Expy: Of Parasite (he can copy the powers of people he drains energy from), with some Venom (being an alien parasite who bonds with host bodies) in there. Flying Brick: He absorbs Fuckwit's strength, flight, and invulnerability and gleefully goes on a rampage with them. Jerkass: A bit moreso than most Fraternity members; he almost manages to try to get Fuckwit to tear off Wesley's armand joins Rictus's coup.

characters.name: Shit-Head
characters.description: Cassandra Truth: Wesley and Fox don't believe him when he claims Rictus had nothing to do with the Killer's death, insisting that they were just as shocked as Seltzer's faction was.It turns out he was telling the truth, as the Killer faked his death to play both sides. Comically Missing the Point: When Wesley calls him fuckface, Shit-Head thinks Wesley had him confused with Fuckwit. The Dragon: To Mr. Rictus. Explain, Explain... Oh, Crap!: As he denies Rictus's involvement in Wesley's dad's murder, he comes to a realization that it was likely Seltzer who was the one who did it.He's ultimately wrong. Expy: Of Clayface; he's a brown, mutated being capable of shifting his form and appearance.The brown isn't mud, though.

characters.name: Seltzer's arch-enemy
characters.description: Alternate Self: Has one in the form ofthe Utopian, who was created by the Millarworld in their subconscious attempt to remember their greatest hero. Arch-Enemy: Of Professor Seltzer, who is an Expy of Lex Luthor. The Cameo: He appears (obscured) in his prime inBig Gameas proof from Bobbie Griffin of the Fraternity's meddling with history. The Cape: Was regarded as the world's greatest hero, and wore a spiffy one that Seltzer took as a trophy after the big battle of '86. Expy Coexistence: The Millarworld has twoSuperman Substitutes, the Utopian and Superior, and its previous iteration supposedly had Superman himself flying around. This is explained to be because the Millarworld's populace was desperately trying to remember him.

characters.name: Alicia Gibson
characters.description: Defector from Decadence: She was a former supervillain who left the life of villainy after becoming a mother, coddling Wesley to the disgust of his father, who wanted his son to follow his legacy. Deliver Us from Evil: Wesley's mother was once a supervillain like his father. However, after he was born she grew disillusioned with the criminal lifestyle, forbidding his father any contact with them andtrying to steer him away from turning out like him. Expy: It's later revealed that she was the Avian's social worker turned girlfriend and may have partook in supervillainy for a bit. This is somewhat reflective ofHarley Quinn. Kick the Morality Pet: The Killer genuinely loved her, but was conflicted between settling down with her or taking every chance he could to kill a superhero. He chose the latter and abandoned his family. My Beloved Smother: She did everything in her power to make sure Wesley grew up with an aversion to violence and confrontation, subconsciously aware of him being susceptible to giving into his supervillain lineage.

characters.name: Lisa
characters.description: Asshole Victim: While Wesley himself is aJerkass, Lisa isn't doing herself any favors by constantly belittling her now ex-boyfriend throughout the first two issues. Cassandra Truth: When Wesley admits to joining a Fraternity of super-criminals and shooting his best friend in the face, Lisa is understandably in disbelief and thinks he's just leaving her for another woman. Admittedly this is partially what's happening, too. Chekhov's Gunman: She returns in Issue #4 on the news where she's interviewed about the murder of Wesley's best friend. It's this that reveals to Wesley that the immunity he'd been enjoying has been rescinded. Domestic Abuse: Lisa is emotionally abusive towards Wesley, basically guilting him multiple times to stay with her despite her admitting to have basically slept with everybody he's known throughout their relationship. When he finally leaves her, she's threatening to slit her wrists to try to make him stay. Informed Flaw: Wesley repeatedly fat-shames her in his inner monologue, but J.G. Jones's art hardly portrays her as anything resembling chubby. Justified as this is meant to indicate how much of Wesley's prejudices were always there, just lacking in any violent outlets.

characters.name: Wesley
characters.description: The main character. Wesley starts out as an account manager whose life sucks: his boss bullies him, his girlfriend cheats on him with his best friend and he takes medications to control his anxiety attacks. But everything changes when he is approached by a woman in a market... Abnormal Ammo: How he killsThe Butcher: by shooting a butcher's steel that got jammed into his gun into him. Action Survivor: He is this before heTook a Level in Badass. Adaptational Attractiveness: Depending on your taste. Wesley in the comic resembles a street punk modeled after Eminem while his movie counterpart is played by the more conventionally attractiveJames McAvoy. Adaptational Heroism: In the comic books, Wesley is a supervillain who happily rapes and slaughters because he believes he has the authority to do as he pleases as a supervillain. This extends even to his pre-assassin day, as this Wesley is already a self-centered asshole even before he joins the Fraternity. In the movie he is more of anAnti-Herowho genuinely believes he's killing bad people.

characters.name: Fox
characters.description: A top ranking member of the Fraternity who recruits Wesley and assists him in most of his missions. When she was a child, her father was burned to death right in front of her eyes. This gave her a lot of insight in her job and why she is an assassin. ...And That Little Girl Was Me: Her backstory, which she explains to Wesley. Armor-Piercing Question: "Why did you come here?". A quite literal example, as she asks this to Wesley while she beats him up, forcing him to reconsider his behavior. Badass Driver: She can pull some insane tricks when behind the wheel. Beauty Is Never Tarnished: The worst injury she gets is some bleeding on her right eye's side. She still looks good with it.

characters.name: Sloan
characters.description: Leader of the Fraternity of assassins. His job is to interpret the codes provided by the threads of the Loom of Fate and assign the discovered names to the assassins to carry on the missions. He was an acquaintance of Wesley's father and trains him to become powerful enough to defeat the rogue agent Cross. Affably Evil: He's a rather polite assassin. Batman Gambit:His whole plan to get Cross killed relied on him knowing that Cross wouldn't kill his own son. Because Destiny Says So: He believes that the Loom chooses their targets and it's an assassin's duty to kill those chosen enemies and fulfill the orders of destiny.Actually a lie. He has been manufacturing his own targets for his own profit. Big Bad:He essentially played Wesley all along and drove most of his story from behind the scenes.

characters.name: Janice
characters.description: Big Eater: A lot of scenes with her involve her stuffing her face. Control Freak: She instantly starts pestering Wesley over surfing the web at work without even seeing his screen, meaning she likely surveils all her employee's screens on her own computer frequently. Evil Redhead: AMean Bosswith red hair. Fat Bastard: She's plump and she's aMean Boss Jerkass: Treats everyone around her with a lot of disrespect.
